events.credibility_reason: Unread student note known only from a snippet; its count (381) conflicts with the 'thousands' attributed to it.
Single independent author, unreviewed; and it concerns odd perfect numbers, not Leinster infinitude.

Unopened snippet-only claim of a landmark (no odd perfect numbers) on an unreviewed preprint server that itself warns against treating it as verified; no uptake; and it is a neighbouring problem anyway.

why: The statement asks only whether infinitely many Leinster groups exist. No event answers or bounds that. Individual examples (Brunault's odd-order group, Nieuwveld's computed list) are finitely many instances. Definitional and order-restriction papers (Leinster 2001, De Medts-Maróti, Baishya) settle no restriction of the infinitude question, so they are none. The Holt Mersenne family reduces infinitude to the open Mersenne-prime question, which is a conditional reduction (none), and its date is unknown. All three in-window events are variants: the almost/quasi-Leinster conditions, and two papers on odd perfect numbers, which bear only on dihedral Leinster groups and not on infinitude. No AI system is credited with mathematics. The Mantovanelli ChatGPT lead (LaTeX, literature, coding) is unverified, and as described it would be none anyway.
doubts: Baishya 2013/2014 and De Medts-Maróti were read only as abstracts. If either proved an unconditional infinite family it would matter, but that would be pre-snapshot, and later sources (Baishya 2019, current Wikipedia) still call the question open.
